arxiv-1608-07800.title: Low-Rank Matrix Completion for Mobile Edge Caching in Fog-RAN via Riemannian Optimization This work is supported by Shanghai Sailing Program No. 16YF1407700.
arxiv-1608-07800.creator: Kai Yang ∗ , Yuanming Shi ∗ , and Zhi Ding † , Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-1608-07800.description: Abstract The upcoming big data era is likely to demand tremendous computation and storage resources for communications. By pushing computation and storage to network edges, fog radio access networks (Fog-RAN) can effectively increase network throughput and reduce transmission latency. Furthermore, we can exploit the benefits of cache enabled architecture in Fog-RAN to deliver contents with low latency.

arxiv-1804-05512.title: Joint Bilateral Filter for Signal Recovery from Phase Preserved Curvelet Coefficients for Image Denoising
arxiv-1804-05512.creator: Supratim Gupta, and Susant Kumar Panigrahi
arxiv-1804-05512.description: Abstract Thresholding of Curvelet Coefficients, for image denoising, drains out subtle signal component in noise subspace. This produces ringing artifacts near edges and granular effect in the denoised image. We found the noise sensitivity of Curvelet phases – in contrast to their magnitude – reduces with higher noise level.

arxiv-1810-11837.title: On the geometric P=W conjecture
arxiv-1810-11837.creator: Mirko Mauri, Enrica Mazzon, Matthew Stevenson
arxiv-1810-11837.description: Abstract . We formulate the geometric P=W conjecture for singular character varieties. We establish it for compact Riemann surfaces of genus one, and obtain partial results in arbitrary genus. To this end, we employ non-Archimedean, birational and degeneration techniques to study the topology of the dual boundary complex of character varieties.

arxiv-2202-05742.title: On the computation of Gröbner bases for matrix-weighted homogeneous systems
arxiv-2202-05742.creator: Thibaut Verron
arxiv-2202-05742.description: Abstract In this paper, we examine the structure of systems that are weighted homogeneous for several systems of weights, and how it impacts the computation of Gröbner bases. We present several linear algebra algorithms for computing Gröbner bases for systems with this structure, either directly or by reducing to existing structures. We also present suitable optimization techniques.

arxiv-2210-12466.title: Design of mid-infrared entangled photon sources using lithium niobate
arxiv-2210-12466.creator: Jin-Long Zhu, Wen-Xin Zhu, Xiao-Tao Shi, Chen-Tao Zhang, Xiangying Hao, Zi-Xiang Yang, Rui-Bo Jin
arxiv-2210-12466.description: Abstract The mid-infrared (MIR) band entangled photon source is vital for the next generation of quantum communication, quantum imaging, and quantum sensing. However, the current entangled states are mainly prepared in visible or near-infrared bands. It is still lack of high-quality entangled photon sources in the MIR band.

arxiv-2311-10176.title: Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning Using Guidance-Informed Hypergraphs
arxiv-2311-10176.creator: Courtney McBeth, James Motes, Isaac Ngui, Marco Morales, Nancy M. Amato
arxiv-2311-10176.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a method for multiple mobile robot motion planning that efficiently plans for robot teams up to an order of magnitude larger than existing state-of-the-art methods in congested settings with narrow passages in the environment.

arxiv-2401-05408.title: Decoding Emotional Valence from Wearables: Can Our Data Reveal Our True Feelings? Conference: 25th International Conference on Mobile Human-Computer Interaction; September 26–29, 2023; Athens, Greece 25th International Conference on Mobile Human-Computer Interaction (MobileHCI ’23 Companion), Septem
arxiv-2401-05408.creator: Michal K. Grzeszczyk, Anna Lisowska, Arkadiusz Sitek, Aneta Lisowska
arxiv-2401-05408.description: Abstract . Automatic detection and tracking of emotional states has the potential for helping individuals with various mental health conditions. While previous studies have captured physiological signals using wearable devices in laboratory settings, providing valuable insights into the relationship between physiological responses and mental states, the transfer of these findings to real-life scenarios is still in its nascent stages.

arxiv-2401-16053.title: Analysis of the spread of SARS-CoV-2 in a hospital isolation room using CFD and Lagrangian Coherent Structures Journal: Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena
arxiv-2401-16053.creator: Narjisse Amahjour, Guillermo García-Sánchez, Makrina Agaoglou, Ana Maria Mancho
arxiv-2401-16053.description: Abstract This research paper presents an analysis of the propagation of the SARS-CoV-2, or other similar pathogens, in a hospital isolation room using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and Lagrangian Coherent Structures (LCS). The study investigates the airflow dispersion and droplets in the room under air conditioning vent and sanitizer conditions.

arxiv-2402-15460.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Michael Sweeting 1,∗ \emailx michael.sweeting@astrazeneca.com, Daniel Slade 2, Dan Jackson 1, and Kristian Brock 3 1 Statistical Innovation, Oncology Biometrics, AstraZeneca, UK 2 Early Oncology Statistics, Oncology Biometrics, AstraZeneca, UK 3 Statistical Innovation, Data Sciences and AI, AstraZen. Triallists wishing to choose a design require knowledge of operating characteristics of competing methods.

arxiv-2406-09757.title: Evaluating LLM-driven User-Intent Formalization for Verification-Aware Languages
arxiv-2406-09757.creator: Shuvendu K. Lahiri
arxiv-2406-09757.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shuvendu K. Lahiri. Verification-aware programming languages such as Dafny and F* provide means to formally specify and prove properties of a program. Although the problem of checking an implementation against a specification can be defined mechanically, there is no algorithmic way of ensuring the correctness of the user-intent formalization for programs — that a specification adheres to the user’s intent behind the program. This is because intent or requirement is expressed informally in natural language and the specification is a formal artefact.

arxiv-2409-10499.title: Partial Distribution Matching via Partial Wasserstein Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2409-10499.creator: Zi-Ming Wang, Nan Xue, Ling Lei, Rebecka Jörnsten, Gui-Song Xia
arxiv-2409-10499.description: Abstract This paper studies the problem of distribution matching (DM), which is a fundamental machine learning problem seeking to robustly align two probability distributions. Our approach is established on a relaxed formulation, called partial distribution matching (PDM), which seeks to match a fraction of the distributions instead of matching them completely.

arxiv-2508-09835.title: Gravitational Wave Signatures of U ​ ( 1 ) X \mathrm{U}(1)_{X} Breaking and Right-Handed Neutrino Dynamics
arxiv-2508-09835.creator: Arnab Chaudhuri, Priya Mishra, and Rukmani Mohanta
arxiv-2508-09835.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arnab Chaudhuri, Priya Mishra, and Rukmani Mohanta. The Standard Model (SM) leaves several fundamental questions unanswered, including the origin of neutrino masses, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and the nature of dark matter. Motivated by these gaps, we investigate an extension of the SM with an additional local U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} gauge symmetry and a complex scalar singlet that spontaneously breaks this symmetry via its vacuum expectation value.

arxiv-2508-10198.title: Digital Contact Tracing: Examining the Effects of Understanding and Release Organization on Public Trust
arxiv-2508-10198.creator: Lucas Draper
arxiv-2508-10198.description: Abstract . Contact tracing has existed in various forms for a very long time. With the rise of COVID-19, the concept has become increasingly important to help slow the spread of the virus. One approach to modernizing contact tracing is to introduce applications that detect all close contacts without individuals having to interact knowingly.

pmc-12595650.creator: Vishal Avinashi, Milli Gupta, Beth A. Payne, Haneen Amhaz, Alisha T. Temirova, Waqqas Afif, Dhandapani Ashok, Janice Barkey, David Burnett, Jonathan W. pmc-12595650.description: BackgroundEosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the esophagus that effects both pediatrics and adult patients in Canada and is increasing in prevalence. No Canadian focused best practice recommendations currently exist to guide clinical practice.MethodsThe study used a modified Delphi technique to develop evidence and expert opinion-based recommendations for providing care for patients with EoE.

pmc-13122406.creator: Elizabeth F. Stone, Daniel Chacreton, Alexandra Jimenez, Shannon Kelly, Ruchika Goel, Jeanne E. Hendrickson, Marianne E. Nellis, Martha Sola-Visner, Oliver Karam, Ravi M. Patel, Sarah Vossoughi, Madhav Vissa, Sarah Wilson, Jeffrey J. VanWormer, Sylvia Titi Singer, Sara Bakhtary, Elliott P. Vichinsky
pmc-13122406.description: This cohort study assesses the epidemiology and rates of transfusion reactions reported in US hospitals among pediatric patients. Introduction Blood transfusion is the most common procedure for hospitalized patients.1,2 Current research suggests that pediatric patients may have a higher rate of transfusion reactions compared with adults, especially for febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reactions (FNHTRs) and allergic transfusion reactions.

pmc-13218176.title: Mapping shared genetic determinants of eGFR and albuminuria with a focus on type 2 diabetes: a large-scale European study
pmc-13218176.creator: Cilia Naaman, Frederik Persson, Thomas Kümler, Simone Theilade, Glenn Chertow, Peter Rossing, Tine Hansen, Tarunveer S Ahluwalia
pmc-13218176.description: Background and hypothesisChronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global health and economic burden, particularly among individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D). According to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes guidelines, key CKD indicators include urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Although independent genetic loci for these traits have been reported, their shared genetic architecture remains insufficiently understood.

pmc-13685295.title: From caregiver burden to psychological resilience and positive emotional outcomes: the effectiveness of innovative psychiatric nursing intervention among family caregivers of patients with bipolar disorder
pmc-13685295.creator: Rania Maher Alhalawany, Yahya Mubark Khatatbeh, Ola Zaher Mansour, Shereen Roushdy Hashem
pmc-13685295.description: BackgroundFamily caregivers of people with bipolar disorder (BD) often experience substantial caregiver burden (CB), lower psychological resilience (PR), and fewer caregiving rewarding feelings (CRF), which generally affect caregiver well-being and patient care. In this study, we assessed the effectiveness of an innovative psychiatric nursing intervention in reducing CB, improving PR, and fostering CRF among family caregivers of patients with BD.

pmc-7618544.title: Lost in Speech: Depressive Rumination and the Dynamics of Inner Silence
pmc-7618544.creator: Unknown
pmc-7618544.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper clarifies the experiential profile of depressive rumination, a form of repetitive and persistent negative thinking that is phenomenologically and aetiologically central in depression. Phenomenological analyses of depression have generally remained too high-level to account for this centrality. Drawing on first-person depression narratives and recent philosophy of psychiatry and psychology, we elucidate an underexplored phenomenological aspect of depressive rumination: a disruption in the capacity for inner silence.
